sections.h2: How large is St. Louis County and who bills its property tax?
sections.html:
St. Louis County is the largest county east of the Mississippi River, and its property tax is billed by the county Auditor, with values set by the Assessor. The county covers 6,860 square miles, 612 of them water, with Duluth as the seat. It takes its name from the St. Louis River, which reaches Lake Superior through the southeast corner. Census QuickFacts puts the density at 32 people per square mile of land.

The county's history page says it holds most of Minnesota's iron mines, which produce 85% of the country's domestic iron, and that the Port of Duluth-Superior is the top tonnage port on the Great Lakes. Courthouses were built in Duluth in 1909 and in Virginia the next year. That two-city layout shows up in county services: the Auditor's office works from the Duluth Courthouse, the Mall-Service Center and the Government Services Center in Virginia, while property tax payments alone can also be made at the Hibbing Courthouse through the County Recorder.

Tax Division contact is 218-726-2383, at 100 N. 5th Ave. W. in Duluth. The county's own assessment page makes clear what the Assessor does and does not do: it estimates market value and classifies property, but it does not collect, calculate or set tax rates.

sections.h2: What does the St. Louis County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
The numbers describe a county with older residents, steady population and moderate home values. Census QuickFacts shows a July 2025 estimate of 200,518 people, almost flat from 200,227 in the April 2020 base.

  • 105,503 housing units and 87,115 households, with 71.2% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $221,400 and median gross rent of $1,013
  • Median household income of $70,069, with 12.7% of people in poverty
  • 23.4% of residents are 65 or older, against 17.8% under 18
  • 412 building permits in 2025 and a mean commute of 19.9 minutes

With 6,247 square miles of land and only 32 residents per square mile, a parcel's location inside the county shapes its value and its tax. That is one reason the assessment and appeal steps below matter to a seller.

sections.h2: What are the St. Louis County tax due dates?
sections.html:
The first half of real estate and personal property tax is due May 15 and the second half October 15. Agricultural second halves are due November 15, and resort property's first half is due May 31. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day, and mailed payments must be postmarked by the date.

Statements are mailed each March, with a statutory deadline of March 31. The county says it is the owner's job to ask the Tax Division for a duplicate if none arrives, and undeliverable mail comes back to the office because it does not forward statements. Partial payments are accepted, and they go first to the penalty accrued for that year.

  • E-check payments online through Paymentus are free, and the Auditor's page lists the other methods with their fees.
  • Drop boxes at county locations take checks or money orders, but no cash.
  • A Truth-in-Taxation notice arrives in November and shows the proposed tax for next year, with dates for local budget meetings.

The county also warns residents about a series of videos claiming a "Senior Homeowner Tax Review Request" tied to a federal law change. It says the programs and forms described do not exist, and it points owners to the real state programs through 218-726-2304.

sections.h2: How does a St. Louis County appeal work?
sections.html:
First speak with your assessor, then work through up to three levels in order, unless you go straight to Minnesota Tax Court. The county's appeals page spells out each level.

  1. City or township Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, which meets in April or May and can change your value or class. Contact the clerk to appear, or send a letter to the clerk to be read at the meeting. The meeting date is the deadline.
  2. County Board of Appeal and Equalization, in the last two weeks of June, made up of members with extensive real estate knowledge. Book a slot through the Clerk of the County Board at 218-726-2385.
  3. Minnesota Tax Court, with until April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

Owners in unorganized townships have no local board and go directly to the county board. The Tax Court has a Small Claims Division for homesteads of any value, other property under $300,000 in market value, and disputes of $5,000 or less including penalty and interest. The Regular Division hears everything else and follows civil procedure rules, so most owners there hire a lawyer. St. Louis County accepts service of Tax Court petitions in person or by email, and the petitioner must file with the district court on time.

sections.h2: What happens if St. Louis County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax turns delinquent on the first business day of the next year, and the county's FAQ describes a slow but firm forfeiture path. For a homestead the process generally takes up to three years.

Steps after St. Louis County property tax goes delinquent (Auditor FAQ)
StepWhat the county says
DelinquencyFirst business day of the year after the tax was due
NoticesTwo newspaper notices, the first by March 20, plus a mailing to the owner
Contest window20 days from the second notice to contest in District Court
Judgment and saleJudgment entered in May, tax judgment sale on the second Monday in May
Redemption3 years for homestead property under the 2014 rule
ForfeitureWhen redemption ends or 60 days after the last warning, whichever is later

An owner can stop the process by paying all delinquent tax and fees at any time before redemption ends. A confession of judgment is the payment plan: the owner pays one tenth of the delinquent tax, penalties and fees plus the current year's tax, and then pays the rest over up to 10 years for a homestead. After forfeiture the owner may be able to repurchase, but there is no guarantee, and the owner receives none of the proceeds if the county sells the land.

sections.h2: What should I do about tax before selling a St. Louis County house?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Division at 218-726-2383 for the current balance, including penalty and any special assessment, before you set a closing date. Special assessments for improvements such as streets appear on the statement as a separate amount, and they are based on the benefit to the property, not its value.

Some parcels here have extra layers. The county's FAQ explains that Tax Increment Financing districts divert part of the tax to the district without changing how the bill is figured, and fiscal disparities share a portion of commercial and industrial growth with the seven-county metropolitan area. If a buyer or title company asks about either, the Auditor's Tax Division can say whether a parcel is affected.

The county's Mortgage/Deed Tax Calculator is linked from the Auditor's page, and the Recorder's office notes that property in the county is either Abstract or Torrens title, which affects how documents are recorded. The office does not give legal advice or help prepare documents, so direct questions to a real estate attorney or a practicing abstractor.

faqs.q: When is St. Louis County property tax due?
faqs.a: May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second half of real estate and personal property tax. Agricultural second halves are due November 15, and the postmark must show the due date or earlier.

faqs.q: Who do I call to schedule a St. Louis County board of appeal hearing?
faqs.a: Call the Clerk of the County Board at 218-726-2385. The County Board of Appeal and Equalization meets in the last two weeks of June, after the city or township board has acted.

faqs.q: Can I pay St. Louis County property tax without a fee?
faqs.a: Yes, e-check payments through Paymentus are free. Other online methods carry fees listed on the Auditor's page, and checks or money orders (no cash) can go in a county drop box.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a St. Louis County homestead after tax delinquency?
faqs.a: Three years for homestead property under the rule effective in 2014. You may pay all delinquent tax and fees at any time before redemption ends, or enter a confession of judgment payment plan.

faqs.q: Where do unorganized township owners appeal in St. Louis County?
faqs.a: Directly to the County Board of Appeal and Equalization, because those townships have no local board. Call the Clerk of the County Board at 218-726-2385 to book a time.
